label: late-position input of c/i/3/x/h/y/0 (end of original or first copy outputs)
explanation: Candidate unit driven jointly by position and input-token identity. By position it fires in two windows: the first two copy steps (recall_idx 1-2, i.e. the steps fed back orig(0)/orig(1); recall_idx 1 alone has 24% rate and 42% of mass) and late original positions (orig_idx >= 6, rate rising to 48% at orig_idx 8). It almost never fires at t <= 4, at the delimiter, or in mid/late copy (recall_idx >= 3, ~1-3%). Within those windows the input token strongly gates it: c, i, 3, x, h, y, 0 have 2-5x lift (c and i alone carry ~40% of mass), and the largest activations (near max) are c or i fed back at recall_idx 1, or i at the last original positions. Activity is more likely in longer sequences (L=9 holds half the mass) and on repeated tokens (in_first=0). Position-only predicate gets 94% mass recall but 19% precision; adding the token set gives F1 ~0.53, so the token dependence is graded rather than a clean set and many window-plus-token steps stay inactive.
